data.title: Calix: Strong Calix One Momentum and Margin Outlook Reinforce Buy Rating at Unchanged $62 Price Target
data.description:
Calix, the Technology sector company, was revisited by a Wall Street analyst today. Analyst Ryan Koontz from Needham maintained a Buy rating on the stock and has a $62.00 price target.

Ryan Koontz has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including the strategic rollout of Calix One and the completion of the firm’s migration to Google Cloud. With dual-cloud expenses now winding down, management expects a meaningful improvement in software and services gross margins, which supports a more attractive earnings profile and justifies maintaining the $62 price target.

Furthermore, early customer uptake of the Calix One platform is exceeding internal forecasts, signaling strong demand for its AI-driven capabilities. Koontz believes the three core pillars of Calix One—subscriber acquisition, ARPU expansion with lower churn, and operating cost efficiencies—should drive faster RPO growth and strengthen the long-term revenue trajectory of CALX, reinforcing his Buy recommendation at an unchanged $62 target.

data.title: Analyst Lifts ELF Beauty Price Target to $118 on Rhode Expansion Through Sephora Europe and New Hair Care Growth
data.description:
Analyst Anna Lizzul of Bank of America Securities reiterated a Buy rating on e.l.f. Beauty, boosting the price target to $118.00.

Anna Lizzul has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including Rhode’s rapid expansion through Sephora Europe, where the brand is set to enter 19 countries and 500 highly productive stores, lifting its global Sephora presence to roughly 40%. This broader distribution is expected to make Sephora one of ELF’s largest retail partners and could eventually add an estimated $150–$200 million in annual Rhode sales, supporting stronger company-wide growth.

Anna Lizzul’s rating is based on the incremental upside from ELF’s new hair care line, which taps into a fast-growing $17 billion U.S. category with products positioned at steep discounts versus prestige competitors yet showing strong consumer purchase intent. Reflecting these growth drivers, she has increased forecasts for Rhode’s fiscal 2027 revenue and total adjusted EBITDA, and raised the stock’s price objective to $118, supported by a DCF valuation that assumes sustained double-digit top-line expansion and a diversified portfolio across cosmetics and skincare.

data.title: Boot Barn: Sales Momentum Rebounds, Q2 Guidance at High End, Buy Rating Reiterated with Unchanged $215 Price Target
data.description:
Janine Stichter, an analyst from BTIG, reiterated the Buy rating on Boot Barn. The associated price target remains the same with $215.00.

Janine Stichter has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including evidence that Boot Barn’s recent sales trends are improving after a temporary slowdown in July. Comparable sales turned positive in August and have stayed solid into September, with strength spread broadly across key merchandise categories, supporting confidence in the underlying demand.

Management now expects fiscal Q2 results to land at the upper end of prior sales and EPS guidance, helped by strong performance from new stores and continued unit expansion. With the company on track to meet its store opening goals and the shares still trading below peer and historical valuation levels, Stichter sees an attractive risk‑reward and keeps the price target unchanged at $215.
